description: Enterprise techniques used by LIGHTRAIL, ATT&CK software S9061 (v1.0)
name: LIGHTRAIL (S9061)

techniques.comment: [LIGHTRAIL](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9061) has communicated over websockets to cloud C2 infrastructure.(Citation: Mandiant_UNC1549_Feb2024)(Citation: Mandiant_UNC1549TTPsTools_Nov2025)

[LIGHTRAIL](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9061) has leveraged hard-coded User Agent strings to blend in with traffic to include `Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/42.0.2311.135 Safari/537.36 Edge/12.10136`.(Citation: Mandiant_UNC1549TTPsTools_Nov2025)(Citation: Mandiant_UNC1549_Feb2024)
[LIGHTRAIL](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9061) has been deployed using a launcher, which has been executed via search-order-hijacking (SoH).(Citation: Mandiant_UNC1549TTPsTools_Nov2025)

[LIGHTRAIL](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9061) has leveraged hard-coded User Agent strings to mimic legitimate browser traffic. (Citation: Mandiant_UNC1549TTPsTools_Nov2025)(Citation: Mandiant_UNC1549_Feb2024)
[LIGHTRAIL](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9061) has leveraged Windows API calls to establish the WebSocket to include `WinHTTP`.(Citation: Mandiant_UNC1549TTPsTools_Nov2025)
[LIGHTRAIL](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9061) has used SOCKS4A proxies to tunnel traffic.(Citation: Mandiant_UNC1549_Feb2024)
[LIGHTRAIL](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9061) has utilized SOCKS4A proxies to communicate with the C2.(Citation: Mandiant_UNC1549_Feb2024)(Citation: Mandiant_UNC1549TTPsTools_Nov2025)
